details:
VIA / SPHEREx is a public-facing explorer that helps people inspect real SPHEREx observations and review astrometric signals in an IRSA catalog.

Users can search NASA/IPAC IRSA for observations near a selected sky position, inspect observation IDs, dates, spectral bands, wavelength ranges and image centers, and open the official data products for further inspection. The interface connects this mission archive workflow with an all-sky map and a review queue built from a one-million-row, user-supplied IRSA catalog export.

For the catalog audit, COBOL validates and packs records, Rust applies deterministic screening rules, and Python/FastAPI and React connect the audit to the web interface. The current screening found 337,546 sources meeting at least one rule and 23,558 meeting both rules. These are statistical review candidates, not confirmed anomalies or discoveries.

An optional local IBM Granite model, run through Ollama, can summarize measurements for human review. It does not set the screening flags or confirm findings. The catalog export alone does not provide the multi-epoch evidence needed to establish motion, so users should inspect the linked observations and their uncertainties before drawing scientific conclusions.

The project uses a transparent, human-in-the-loop approach: it combines legacy COBOL data validation, Rust screening, public NASA/IPAC archive access and optional local AI assistance in one accessible interface.

Source code: https://github.com/WolfShaddows/VIA-SPHEREx-Mission-Explorer

Data provenance: https://github.com/WolfShaddows/VIA-SPHEREx-Mission-Explorer/blob/main/DATA_PROVENANCE.md
